## Result

- Skill: proposal-review
- Review status: approved
- Vision alignment: aligned
- Material findings: none
- Open blockers: none for this proposal assessment.
- Proposal readiness: revised direction is sufficiently valuable, bounded and feasible for the owning Design stage.
- Immediate next stage: return to Route for the separately authorized Design package review.
- Automatic downstream handoff: none from this assessment; this save does not start or approve Design Review.
- Claim limitations: this is a fresh assessment of the revised proposal only. It does not approve the already-authored Design package, deletion inventory, implementation, release, adoption or final verification. Prior proposal-review remains unchanged and stale for current reliance.

## Review Dimensions

- Challenge: pass. Fragmented delivery contracts and duplicate active installation mechanisms justify consolidation. The original two-candidate System description is the pre-change problem basis; System's newer prospective combined-model text reflects this initiative, without claiming adoption.
- Goals: pass. One delivery owner and a coherent retained-target install path remain the outcomes; user-requested state/upgrade simplification is now expressly part of those outcomes.
- Scope: pass. The original model, superseded-source removal, OpenCode withdrawal and bounded stale-script cleanup all remain in scope. The new state-writing/automatic-upgrade withdrawal covers opt-in and specialized replacement paths, avoiding a defaults-only interpretation.
- Governing principle: pass. One delivery owner remains distinct from local installation permission and public publication authorization.
- Direction: pass. Distribution coherently covers canonical transformation through safe additive installation. Skill owns content, Release owns publication, and existing state remains read-only safety input. Identical files remain unchanged, conflicts stop and manual replacement requires explicit operator action.
- Feasibility: pass. One embedded Feasibility assessment identifies current generator/manifest/installer boundaries, legacy state/integrity safeguards and affected Release support obligations. Target-native init already has an install-only mode with byte-preservation and safety reads (TNI-R14–24); TNI-R25–28 and current CLI --write-state/managed-replacement paths demonstrate the expressly removed capability. The refinement narrows writing behavior without requiring a new platform. Exact conflict, old-state and recovery dispositions remain Design work.
- Material impact: pass. Removal of OpenCode, opt-in state creation and automatic managed upgrades is explicitly disclosed as a public compatibility break and requested decision. Preserved historical packages are not continuing support. Manual replacement and the applicable Release versioning dependency are visible.
- Vision alignment: pass; aligned. An inspectable delivery contract and explicit safety/compatibility boundaries support trustworthy, reviewable engineering. Removal of installer-created state does not remove Workflow/Record Format engineering records or their traceability obligations.
- Downstream authority: pass. Design owns concrete source/consumer reconciliation and transition behavior; Delivery owns sequencing and proof. The proposal does not settle the exact deletion list, rewrite historical evidence, grant publication authority or claim the existing Design draft has passed review.
- Requested decision: pass. Approval is explicitly sought for the full original scope plus removal of managed-state creation and automatic upgrades, with retained-target safety and historical preservation.

## Scope Preservation Review

- Scope-preservation result: pass. All four original outcomes remain required in this initiative. The later user refinement is expressly added, with safe install-only delivery and read-only old-state protection as its intended outcome. No goal is deferred or silently narrowed. Script cleanup remains limited to the delivery/withdrawal responsibility; no unrelated repository-wide cleanup is implied.

## Recommended Proposal Edits

- Recommended edits: none required for direction approval.

## Recommendation

- Recommendation: approve the revised proposal. Independently review the exact affected Design package against this revised direction before Delivery relies on it. That review must assess the concrete managed-upgrade/state-writing retirement, old-state safety, release smoke changes and legacy-source dispositions; this proposal approval does not substitute for it.

## Specialized-gate group

- Active gate predicates: scope_budget_context=true; vision_exception_context=false; standing_artifact_context=false.
- Gate outcomes: pass. Core work, separate implementation slices and shared dependencies remain explicit. The nonstandard treatment 'explicit user refinement' is accepted because its row also says in scope, names the exact removal/safety outcome, and the following paragraph unambiguously includes it in this initiative; it creates no hidden deferral or downstream ambiguity.
- Trigger ambiguity: none.

## Durable-recording group

- Recording status: recorded through review record; successful persistence is required before reliance.
- Recording blocker: none.
- Record path: docs/changes/2026-09-10-distribution-model-and-opencode-retirement/reviews/proposal-review-r2.json
- Finding-record paths: none.

## Formal-review group

- Review ID: proposal-review-r2
- Review record: docs/changes/2026-09-10-distribution-model-and-opencode-retirement/reviews/proposal-review-r2.json
- Governed change identity: 2026-09-10-distribution-model-and-opencode-retirement
- Classification: formal-lifecycle/manual, bounded delegated reassessment; durable_recording_context=true; PRR1G-recorded-context-gated.
- Independence: this separate distribution-proposal-reviewer agent authored neither the original proposal nor its state/upgrade revision. The parent authored the initial proposal as distribution-proposal-author and the user-requested revision as distribution-design-author. Reviewer edits are confined to assessment evidence; separate agent authorship, rather than a role rename or passing check, establishes independence.
- History: proposal-review assessed the earlier sha256:dd2f845191a496a1947386ea5e72384df11228cce87a7cfca25bf766ffe262fa subject and remains untouched with stale applicability. This record independently assesses the complete revised proposal at its new identity; no old judgment is retargeted.
- Evidence scope: complete revised proposal, prior judgment and selected current registry declarations; current standing authority and vision; bounded linked System/Release/source sections and current generator/CLI boundaries. The current System/Release amendments remain prospective; they are inspected for compatibility context, not treated as already-adopted approval.
- Known validation limitation: selected registry context contains a failed design-source-prose-baseline result reporting 33 pre-existing legacy prose errors and zero introduced findings, plus stale older Design evidence. This assessment neither reuses those results as passes nor waives downstream Design/Verify obligations. They do not make the proposal's stated direction or bounded feasibility unassessable. No runtime validation or whole Design review is claimed here.

## Inspected basis identities

Only the proposal is the assessment subject. The other identities are governing, factual or historical-review basis and are not separately approved by this record.
